text:
maria: Quick sync — we need a concrete bench design for the KV-cache + quant + speculative experiments. Goal: apples-to-apples numbers so we can decide an actual regression gate for the rollout.

maria: TL;DR: replay harness, fixed kernel selection, same model weights, sweep quant profiles (fp16, int8, nf4), and speculative on/off. Collect latency distribution, tokens/sec, and perplexity/LL on eval set.

tom: +1. Important bit: kernel selection must be deterministic. If the runtime picks kernels based on heuristics, we should force a kernel config for each experiment (kernel_override). Otherwise results are noisy.

jen: Agree. Also add: same sequence-length distribution and same prefix cache warmup process for replay vs synthetic. We saw warmup mismatch last week that blew p95.

sam: quick question — for speculative decoding, are we using our tiny spec-model (3B) vs main (13B) config? Need to log spec accuracy and wasted tokens.

maria: Use the 3B as the spec-model for the speculative runs. Capture: spec_accept_rate, wasted_token_ratio, and end-to-end latency delta.

liam: For quant profiles let's be explicit: baseline fp16, int8 (static per-layer), nf4 (GPTQ-like), and an aggressive 4-bit asymmetric run. Label them q_fp16, q_int8, q_nf4, q_4bitA.

tom: Suggested harness command (repro-friendly):
```
./harness/run_loadtest \
  --mode replay \
  --trace traces/2026-11-04-replay.json \
  --model-rev v2.3.1 \
  --kernel-override kernels/kepler_opt.json \
  --quant-profile q_nf4 \
  --speculative-model models/spec-3b \
  --concurrency 64 \
  --collect metrics.json
```
Please include the `--kernel-override` and `--model-rev` flags in every job.

jen: Also capture KV cache hit/miss per-request and cold-start distribution. Add a small cold-run bucket (~5% of requests) to simulate cache churn.

sam: For apples-to-apples with synthetic: run the same trace but replay-inserted synthetic user IDs so batching characteristics match. Synthetic-only (purely synthetic arrival process) can be a separate axis but label it.

maria: On quality metrics: run eval set (1k prompts) for each config and log token-level logprobs and F1 on structured outputs. We'll compute delta-LL and a small human spot-check sample for hallucinations. Regression gate needs both perf and quality.

liam: Proposal for regression thresholds: block rollout if p95 latency increases > 5% AND relative eval LL drops > 1.5% OR spec_wasted_tokens > 8% (when speculative enabled). Those are conservative; we can tighten later.

tom: I prefer threshold gating to be: either perf regression OR quality regression alone should block. If perf only (latency + cost) then can trigger canary but not full block. Want to avoid false positives from tiny LL noise.

jen: +1 on separate gates: quality gate (delta-LL, hallucination rate) must be stricter. Perf gate can be multi-level: minor regression -> alert, major regression -> block. We should encode that in the PR template.

maria: Perf-bot — run quick smoke for q_nf4 vs fp16 on staging GPUs? (small replay, 200 reqs).

perf-bot: starting smoke run: job_id=smoke-1876509876-1. kernels=kep_opt.json quant=q_nf4 concurrency=16. ETA ~2m.

perf-bot: smoke results uploaded: https://perf.internal/smoke-1876509876-1 — p50: 28ms (fp16=26ms), p95: 90ms (fp16=85ms), spec_accept=0.62, wasted_tokens=5.3% 

sam: Not surprising. Need full trace results though. Small-run noise is high.

liam: For final runs, we should capture per-kernel timing breakdown (attention, matmul, kv_read, kv_write) and the compile flags used. That will help correlate quant artifacts to specific kernels.

maria: Agreed. Also version everything: harness commit hash, runtime image tag, kernel bundle hash, model rev. Put them in metrics.json header.

tom: Action items:
- maria: write bench PR with the experiment matrix and thresholds (include the command examples above).
- tom: add kernel_override support to the dashboard so we can filter results by kernel.
- jen: add KV cold-run injection to harness (5% by default).
- sam: run the full sweep and upload outputs.

maria: I'll draft the PR today and include the gating logic. Will ping when ready for review.

jen: Thanks — also add a short note in the PR about measurement reproducibility (random seeds, cpu pinning, no background jobs).

maria: Will do. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: noted: CI note added to job: reproducibility=true, seed=42, cpu-isolate=true

sam: Ok I'm starting the long runs now — will post results as they finish.

maria: 👍 thanks everyone.
